title: Create a Home View
description: Write a simple view that returns a welcome message and map it to the root URL.
problemStatement:
## Your Mission

In your Django project, create a new app named `pages`. Inside it, write a view called `home` that returns an `HttpResponse` with the text "Welcome to My Site!".

Then, configure the URLs so that when a user visits the root URL (e.g., `http://127.0.0.1:8000/`), they see that message.

> **Hint**: You'll need to create a `urls.py` inside the `pages` app and include it in the project's main `urls.py`.
hints: Don't forget to add 'pages' to INSTALLED_APPS.
In `pages/urls.py`, define a pattern for `''` that points to the view.
The view should accept a `request` parameter and return `HttpResponse(...)`.
expectedOutput: When you visit `http://127.0.0.1:8000/`, the page displays "Welcome to My Site!".
solutionCode:
# pages/views.py
from django.http import HttpResponse

def home(request):
    return HttpResponse("Welcome to My Site!")

# pages/urls.py
from django.urls import path
from . import views

urlpatterns = [
    path('', views.home, name='home'),
]

# project/urls.py
from django.contrib import admin
from django.urls import path, include

urlpatterns = [
    path('admin/', admin.site.urls),
    path('', include('pages.urls')),
]

# settings.py – add 'pages' to INSTALLED_APPS
